headline: How to Introduce Your Expertise So AI Search Can Categorize It
blog_article:
Most About pages, LinkedIn summaries, and speaker bios are written for human warmth.

That is not enough anymore.

AI search does not categorize you by how sincere you sound. It categorizes you by the signals you repeat: the problem you solve, the people you solve it for, and the method you use to solve it.

If your public profile says, “passionate about helping businesses grow,” you have not given AI search a useful category. You have given it a personality statement.

Use this structure instead:

[problem you solve] + [who has it] + [how you solve it differently]

In that order.

Here is the Presence Script.

## 1. Name the problem first.

Write the specific business problem you want to be known for solving before you introduce your background, personality, or values.

Why this works: AI search needs category signals, and the problem is usually the strongest signal.

Weak version:
“I’m passionate about helping businesses grow.”

Stronger version:
“I help B2B service businesses fix inconsistent visibility.”

## 2. Identify the buyer category.

State the type of business or buyer you work with in plain language.

Why this works: AI search needs to understand who your expertise is relevant to, not just what you care about.

Weak version:
“I work with ambitious founders and growing teams.”

Stronger version:
“I work with small B2B service businesses, including agencies, consultants, and MSPs.”

## 3. Describe the struggle they already recognize.

Use language your buyer would use when describing the problem internally.

Why this works: Search visibility improves when your expertise matches the wording buyers use before they contact you.

Weak version:
“I help companies unlock their potential.”

Stronger version:
“I work with service business owners whose marketing goes quiet when client work gets busy.”

## 4. Add your distinct approach.

Explain how you solve the problem differently from the usual options.

Why this works: The approach separates you from every other provider in the same broad category.

Weak version:
“I offer strategic marketing support tailored to your needs.”

Stronger version:
“I build repeatable presence systems so visibility does not depend on the owner having free time.”

## 5. Combine the pieces into one category-rich statement.

Use this structure:

“I work with [type of business] who struggle with [specific problem] by [specific approach].”

Why this works: The sentence gives AI search a clean category signal and gives human buyers an immediate reason to keep reading.

Ready-to-use template:

“I work with [type of business] who struggle with [specific problem] by [specific approach or method].”

Examples:

“I work with B2B consultants who struggle to stay visible between referrals by turning their expertise into a repeatable content system.”

“I work with MSPs who struggle to explain their value before a sales call by building category-specific messaging for their website, LinkedIn, and sales materials.”

“I work with agency owners whose marketing disappears when delivery gets busy by creating a practical visibility rhythm their team can maintain.”

## 6. Repeat the same signal across every public touchpoint.

Use the same core wording on your About page, LinkedIn summary, website bio, speaker bio, podcast bio, newsletter footer, and directory profiles.

Why this works: One strong sentence is useful, but repeated category signals create Compound Presence.

Do not write one version for your website, another vague version for LinkedIn, and a third personality-driven version for your bio.

Use a consistent base statement and adapt lightly for context.

Base statement:
“I work with B2B service businesses who struggle with inconsistent visibility by building repeatable presence systems.”

LinkedIn version:
“I work with B2B service businesses whose visibility depends too much on the owner’s spare time. I help build repeatable presence systems across the places buyers check before they reach out.”

About page version:
“Never Blank works with small B2B service businesses — agencies, consultants, and MSPs — that go quiet when delivery gets busy. We build repeatable presence systems that keep the business visible across relevant buyer touchpoints.”

Short bio version:
“I help B2B service businesses replace owner-dependent marketing with repeatable presence systems.”

The point is not to sound identical everywhere.

The point is to make your category unmistakable everywhere.

If AI search has to guess what you do, who you help, or where to place you, your presence is carrying debt.

Fix the sentence.

Then repeat it until the market can categorize you before they ever contact you.
linkedin_post:
Wrong:

“I’m passionate about helping businesses grow.”

Right:

“I work with B2B service businesses whose marketing goes quiet when client work gets busy by building repeatable presence systems.”

The first sentence has warmth.

The second has category signal.

That matters because AI search is not only reading your About page for personality. It is trying to categorize your expertise.

If your LinkedIn summary, website bio, About page, and content bio are full of phrases like:

- passionate about helping businesses grow
- empowering founders
- unlocking potential
- strategic partner for success

…you are making the categorization job harder.

Use this instead:

“I work with [type of business] who struggle with [specific problem] by [specific approach].”

Examples:

“I work with B2B consultants who struggle to stay visible between referrals by turning their expertise into a repeatable content system.”

“I work with MSPs who struggle to explain their value before a sales call by building category-specific messaging for their website, LinkedIn, and sales materials.”

“I work with agency owners whose marketing disappears when delivery gets busy by creating a visibility rhythm their team can maintain.”

Then repeat the same category signal across your:

- LinkedIn summary
- About page
- website bio
- podcast bio
- newsletter footer
- speaker profile
- directory listings

Not word-for-word.

Consistently enough that AI search, referral partners, and future buyers understand the same thing:

what problem you solve, who you solve it for, and why your approach is different.

That is Compound Presence.

A repeated clear signal compounds.

The same clear signal repeated across public touchpoints becomes Compound Presence.
